title: Weld Neck Flange Dimensions
description: Covers standard and long weld neck flange types, common materials, the ASME B16.5 dimensional parameters, class ratings and typical applications.
content:
Weld neck flanges (WN flanges) are a type of flange that is integral to the piping system, connecting pipes, valves, pumps, and other equipment. These flanges are designed to transfer stress to the pipe, reducing high-stress concentrations at the flange base.

Types of Weld Neck Flanges

Standard Weld Neck Flanges

The most common type, featuring a long, tapered hub that provides reinforcement and reduces stress concentration.

Long Weld Neck Flanges

Have an extended neck and are typically used as nozzles for columns or barrels in industrial applications. They come in two designs: Equal LWN Barrel and LWN Heavy Barrel.

Material Specifications

  • Carbon Steel: Commonly used grades include ASTM A181 and ASTM A105, known for strength and temperature resistance.
  • Stainless Steel: Includes grades like ASTM A182, F304, and 316L, offering excellent corrosion resistance and durability.
  • Duplex Steel: UNS S31803 is a popular duplex steel, providing high strength and resistance to stress corrosion cracking.
  • Nickel Alloys: Materials like Inconel 600 and 625 are used for superior resistance to oxidation and corrosion in extreme environments.

Dimensional Standards

Weld neck flanges are standardized according to ASME B16.5, ensuring uniformity in dimensions and tolerances. Key dimensional parameters include: Nominal Pipe Size (NPS), Outside Diameter (OD), Flange Thickness (T), Bolt Circle Diameter (BCD), Number of Bolt Holes, and Raised Face (RF) Dimensions.

Class Ratings

Class ratings indicate the pressure-temperature rating of the flange. Common classes include 150, 300, 600, 900, 1500, and 2500. As the class rating increases, the dimensions, especially the thickness and bolt size, change to accommodate higher pressure and temperature.

Example Dimensions

For a Class 150 weld neck flange:

  • 1/2" NPS: OD 3.50" (88.9 mm), flange thickness 0.38" (9.7 mm), bolt circle 2.38" (60.5 mm), 4 bolt holes at 0.62" (15.7 mm)
  • 2" NPS: OD 6.00" (152.4 mm), flange thickness 0.69" (17.5 mm), bolt circle 4.75" (120.7 mm), 4 bolt holes at 0.75" (19.1 mm)

Full Class 150 dimensions

These tables are crucial for ensuring proper fit and function in piping systems.

Installation and Usage

Proper installation involves welding them to the pipe. The taper of the neck allows for smooth transition of stress from the flange to the pipe, ensuring the flange can handle high pressure and temperature variations without failing.

Applications

  • Oil and Gas: For pipelines and processing plants
  • Chemical Processing: Where high-pressure and corrosive environments are common
  • Power Generation: In steam, hydro, and nuclear plants

Conclusion

Weld neck flanges are essential components in various industries due to their strength, reliability, and ability to handle high-stress applications. Understanding their dimensions, material specifications, and proper installation methods is crucial for ensuring the safety and efficiency of piping systems.
